stem:
A 3-year-old presents because her parents have noticed a new head tilt. She is otherwise well and thriving. Examination is normal apart from the head tilt. Photos from infancy show normal head posture.

What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Discharge the patient with an outpatient physiotherapy referral
Request an urgent MRI of the brain

explanation: This child has an isolated acquired head tilt with a normal examination and no red flags. The most likely diagnosis is benign torticollis/postural preference, so initial management is conservative with outpatient follow-up and physiotherapy rather than urgent neuroimaging or invasive testing.
rationale: The item appears to have mixed content from a prior neurology case, but the available answer choices clearly fit the head-tilt vignette. The best single answer is conservative management with physiotherapy referral.

optionExplanations.A: Lumbar puncture is not indicated without signs of infection, raised intracranial pressure, or neurological concern.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: isolated head tilt in a well child with a normal examination is usually managed conservatively with physiotherapy and follow-up.
optionExplanations.C: A cervical spine x-ray is not the first-line test in an otherwise well child with no trauma or focal neurological findings.
optionExplanations.D: Urgent brain MRI is unnecessary in the absence of neurological deficits, developmental regression, or other red flags.

Instructions

Question 4 - 6 relate to this quiz

Case 2

A 5-year old girl is brought in by her mother to see you because her teacher has been concerned that she has been having ‘day-dreams’ in choir practise and also during class. Her mother has also noted ‘day dreams’ which have been occurring mid-sentence associated with staring off in the distance. The ‘day dreams’ last a few seconds and then she is back to normal and continues on with her sentence. She doesn’t fall and doesn’t get sleepy after the events. She has no colour change. The girl is otherwise developmentally normal and got a good mid-year report from school. On examination her height and weight are on the 75

th

centile. She has a completely normal examination. You get the patient to blow up a balloon in your office and she has a staring spell that lasts 5seconds before she completely recovers.
